title: From the Editor — Dead Weight in the Basin
settingText: Cinder Basin seen from high and far: pale basin floor, heat shimmer, a small patchwork traveling camp beneath black half-buried Sunforge ribs. The road arrives from the lower corner. No identifiable faces; the visual should feel like a place already waiting.
summary: Art-directed opening editorial splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 2. Entice the reader, establish the live pressure and world feeling, and preserve the story page-one reveal.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ART-DIRECTED SPLASH. Use one cinematic illustration rather than sequential panels. Reserve a large, deliberately quiet field for the supplied editorial body copy. The illustration supports the text without depicting the next issue's reveal literally.

LETTERING LAYOUT. Treat the supplied CAPTION lines as designed editorial typography, not speech balloons: strong heading, readable body copy, generous leading and margins, and a prominent final hook line. Do not invent any additional text, logos, signage, credits or slogans.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: One wrong name can be an accident.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: By the time Brandon Mack leaves the Last Drop, the accident has acquired witnesses, enemies, a hero, and a road of its own.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: He has also acquired Jessie and Eva, though he may dispute the wording.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Sunfields do not care.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Out here, stories move faster than people, and a reputation does not need permission from the person wearing it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Cinder Basin is ahead.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A camp there has been waiting a long time for somebody.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Brandon has never met them.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That may not matter.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: — Jeff Hines

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Star Splitter Visions

No spoilers beyond what the supplied editorial text itself implies. Do not visually reveal the next issue's identity mistake, confrontation, culprit, resolution or other first-page surprise.

title: Cinder Basin
summary: The trio reaches Cinder Basin looking for water and shade. Los Lagartos are visibly in the middle of an internal dispute, but nobody has yet addressed the travelers.

panelPlan.text: Wide approach into Cinder Basin: white alkali dust, patched shade, tethered mounts and a traveling camp arranged around half-buried black ribs. Two clusters of Los Lagartos argue across a cookfire while children and workers continue ordinary camp life around them.
Jessie slows the rig at the camp edge. Eva studies the argument. Brandon studies the water barrels.
A Sand Rider on watch notices them and signals inward. Several heads turn at once.
Brandon steps down with an empty canteen. The camp goes quiet in stages rather than all at once.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: They're already fighting about something.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Then don't volunteer us for it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm volunteering for water.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That worked well last time.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Last time I got water.

title: General Diaz
summary: An older Lagarto recognizes Brandon as General Diaz. Relief and anger split the camp before Brandon can finish denying the name.

panelPlan.text: An older Lagarto rises slowly from the communal table, staring at Brandon with stunned relief.
He addresses Brandon as General Diaz. One side of the camp stands; the opposing side stiffens and reaches for belts and chair backs rather than weapons.
Jessie immediately shifts one step back toward the rig. Eva stays still, watching who reacts to the name and how.
Brandon keeps the empty canteen visible and points toward the water table.

dialogueInline.speaker: Older Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: General Diaz. We were told you were coming.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm Brandon Mack.

dialogueInline.speaker: Older Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: You took your time.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That would be Diaz's business.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Mine is water.

title: The Man They Expected
summary: Los Lagartos have been given enough detail about Diaz's expected return that Brandon's denial sounds like confirmation rather than contradiction.

panelPlan.text: Several Lagartos compare Brandon openly with remembered details: black hair, dark coat, age roughly right, no recognizable family tokens. Their certainty is social, not forensic.
A woman from the angry cluster points out that Diaz was older. Someone answers that years on the road change a man.
Eva notices a more disturbing detail: people were apparently warned that Diaz would deny the name.
Brandon fills his canteen while the argument about who he is continues behind his shoulder.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: The preacher said you'd deny it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Convenient preacher.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Did he say anything else?

dialogueInline.speaker: Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: Dark coat. Black hair. Travels light. Watches exits.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That describes half the road.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Not the denial.

title: Water First
summary: Sand Rider gives the travelers the immediate context: Diaz disappeared years ago after holding together a fragile political compromise, and the camp has never agreed on what should replace him.

panelPlan.text: At the water table, Sand Rider pours for Brandon and speaks without ceremony while the larger camp watches from a respectful distance.
He points out two clusters: an older blood-claim faction and a younger group backing a leader chosen by vote.
Jessie asks whether Diaz is dead. Sand Rider answers that Diaz disappeared on a route and never returned; no body came back.
Eva realizes the camp has been living with an unresolved absence long before Brandon arrived.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sand Rider
dialogueInline.text: Diaz kept both sides angry enough to stay together.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: What happened to him?

dialogueInline.speaker: Sand Rider
dialogueInline.text: Went south three years ago. His mount came back. He did not.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: And now somebody told you he was returning.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sand Rider
dialogueInline.text: Told us a man matching him would come through.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: You got the wrong man.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sand Rider
dialogueInline.text: I believe you. That will not help much.

title: Two Claims
summary: The camp puts its real dispute in front of Brandon: whether an old blood claim outranks a leader chosen by the traveling community.

panelPlan.text: The communal table becomes a hearing despite Brandon's refusal. One faction presents a worn family token tied to Diaz's old command; the other presents a tally board from a recent vote.
An older claimant argues that Diaz promised authority would stay within a particular family line.
A younger elected representative argues that the people who actually travel, repair, cook and scout already voted.
Eva watches speakers edit their words whenever they look at Brandon, trying to sound like people Diaz would approve of.

dialogueInline.speaker: Older Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: Diaz said the line holds until he returns.

dialogueInline.speaker: Younger Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: He also said the camp belongs to the people walking with it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Those sound like two different arguments.

dialogueInline.speaker: Older Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: Which one stands?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Why would I decide that?

dialogueInline.speaker: Younger Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: Because they told us Diaz was coming to settle it.

title: The Head Chair
summary: Los Lagartos keep placing Brandon in Diaz's old position. Brandon physically removes himself from the role, but the gesture is interpreted as a test of the community.

panelPlan.text: Someone sets Diaz's old chair at the head of the table. Brandon moves it to the side and sits on a water crate.
The factions immediately debate what the movement means. One calls it humility; another calls it contempt for blood privilege.
Eva sits near Brandon and quietly translates the interpretations accumulating around his every move.
Brandon stands again and carries the chair completely away from the table.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: They think moving the chair was a statement.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: It was. I don't want the chair.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That is not what they heard.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then they need better ears.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: They already turned a denial into proof.

title: What Refusal Sounds Like
summary: Brandon's refusal keeps producing authority because both factions need Diaz more than they need evidence that Brandon is him.

panelPlan.text: Brandon walks toward the rig. People from both factions follow, each asking a different version of the same question.
Jessie opens the driver's side and signals that they can leave immediately.
A family with children blocks no path but asks Brandon whether they should move their camp if the dispute turns violent.
Brandon stops because the question is about immediate safety rather than status.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: If the blood claim is wrong, say it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Another Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: If the vote is wrong, say that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I don't know enough to bless either one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Parent
dialogueInline.text: Do we move the children before dark?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: If you think somebody here is willing to shoot over this, yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That answer they can use.

title: The Woman Behind Them
summary: Eva notices Raina questioning people at the camp edge and realizes someone is studying Brandon's effect on the dispute rather than participating in it.

panelPlan.text: At the camp edge, Raina questions a Lagarto while taking compact notes. Her fitted field gear and brass optics mark her as a traveler with purpose, not part of the community.
Eva watches from behind a shade post. Jessie notices Eva's attention and follows her sightline.
Raina closes the notebook, meets Eva's stare and approaches instead of pretending not to have been watching.
Jessie steps beside Eva, not in front of her, making the boundary clear without turning it into a standoff.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: You're traveling with him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Who are you?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Raina James.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Why are you asking about Brandon?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Because people keep giving me other names for his face.

title: Four Names
summary: Raina reveals that Brandon's face is attached to more identities than Eva and Jessie have encountered, but she refuses to explain how she collected them.

panelPlan.text: Raina opens a small notebook only enough to show four separate name entries beside rough descriptions, keeping the lower notes covered with her thumb.
Eva recognizes Brannock and Diaz but not the other two names.
Jessie asks the practical question: whether Raina believes Brandon is dangerous. Raina cannot answer cleanly.
Raina looks past them toward Brandon, who is helping move a family's bedrolls away from the dispute.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I have four names and one face.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: We've heard two.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Then you just got here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Do you think he's dangerous?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I think he's lying about something.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That wasn't my question.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: I don't know yet.

title: A Question Raina Won't Answer
summary: Eva tries to learn where Raina's other names came from. Raina deflects, and Brandon finally sees that the stranger has been following his trail.

panelPlan.text: Eva asks where Raina got the names. Raina says from people with reasons to remember them, not from one source.
Jessie asks whether Raina has spoken to Brandon directly. Raina says she has asked him his name before and received the same answer.
Brandon approaches with the relocated bedrolls and recognizes Raina as someone he has seen at previous stops or on the road, though never close enough to speak.
Raina chooses not to confront him in the middle of the camp dispute and steps away.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Where did the other names come from?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Different places.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Have you asked him?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: He says Brandon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: You're the woman from the north road.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Among other roads.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: If you want to ask me something, ask.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Not while everybody here is listening for the answer they want.

title: A Vote Nobody Wants
summary: The camp reconvenes because both factions believe Brandon's presence makes delay impossible. Sand Rider warns him that refusing to choose may only push the dispute toward violence.

panelPlan.text: The communal table is reset without the head chair, but both factions return in greater numbers.
Sand Rider tells Brandon the younger faction already won a narrow vote; the older faction refuses to recognize it without Diaz.
Brandon asks why the elected side needs his approval if it trusts the vote.
The question lands harder on the elected side than on the blood claimants.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sand Rider
dialogueInline.text: The vote happened. Twenty-nine to twenty-six.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then why am I sitting here?

dialogueInline.speaker: Younger Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: Because they won't honor it without Diaz.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Do you honor it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Younger Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: We do.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then start there.

title: The Gun
summary: The argument finally crosses the line everyone has been predicting when a younger supporter draws on an older rival across the meal fire.

panelPlan.text: The debate shifts from legitimacy to insult. An older man calls the vote a theft carried out while elders were away.
A younger supporter stands too quickly, chair scraping hard against the ground. Sand Rider turns before the weapon is visible.
The younger man draws a sidearm across the campfire.
Brandon's hand closes around the tin cup already beside him, not his own weapon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Older Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: You counted people who had no right to decide.

dialogueInline.speaker: Younger Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: They travel with us. They bury ours. They decide.

dialogueInline.speaker: Older Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: Diaz would have thrown your tally in the fire.

dialogueInline.speaker: Younger Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: Diaz isn't here.

title: Tin Cup
summary: Brandon stops the shooting with the nearest object, and Sand Rider restrains the gunman. The action is quick, physical and entirely about preventing a killing.

panelPlan.text: The gun clears leather. Brandon strikes the muzzle sideways with the tin cup before it levels.
The shot goes into empty ground beside the fire. People recoil from dust and sparks.
Sand Rider drives the shooter's wrist to the table and removes the weapon.
Brandon checks the older target for injury before looking at the gunman.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Anybody hit?

dialogueInline.speaker: Older Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: No.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sand Rider
dialogueInline.text: I have the gun.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Keep it.

title: What Diaz Would Do
summary: Los Lagartos immediately convert Brandon's intervention into a supposed ruling, proving that even useful action can be absorbed by the role they need him to play.

panelPlan.text: The camp remains frozen after the shot. Someone from the elected side says Brandon protected their man; an elder says Diaz always stopped bloodshed before judgment.
Brandon points out that he stopped one person from shooting another, not one faction from winning.
Sand Rider quietly tells Brandon they will call the action a judgment regardless.
Eva sees Brandon's frustration sharpen because the interpretation could change the camp's future.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: He chose.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: He was about to shoot a man.

dialogueInline.speaker: Older Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: Diaz always protected the camp before he ruled.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then Diaz and I agree on one thing. Don't shoot people across dinner.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sand Rider
dialogueInline.text: They will call that a judgment.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then help me make it harder.

title: Not a Judgment
summary: Brandon publicly separates the immediate safety decision from the camp's political dispute and refuses to let his action decide a question he does not understand.

panelPlan.text: Brandon stands where everyone can hear him but remains outside the head position.
He asks the restrained gunman whether he drew because of the vote or because he was angry. The man admits he was angry.
Brandon asks the older target whether being shot at makes the blood claim true. The older man refuses the premise.
Jessie watches the crowd begin to distinguish the shooting from the succession dispute.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Stopping that shot settled one thing. He doesn't get to kill you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: It did not settle who leads this camp.

dialogueInline.speaker: Older Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: Then settle that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: No.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: You already have a vote. You also have a man who ignored it. Those are your facts.

title: Where Diaz Went
summary: Brandon finally asks the question the camp has avoided: what authority can Diaz still exercise if he has been gone for years and may be dead.

panelPlan.text: The light has shifted toward evening. The restrained gunman is released without his weapon and sent away from the table.
Brandon asks for the last confirmed fact about Diaz. Different people offer memories until Sand Rider gives the clean version: south route, mount returned, Diaz did not.
Brandon asks how long the camp plans to postpone its decisions for a man nobody can find.
Eva watches the question land as grief before it lands as politics.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Where is Diaz?

dialogueInline.speaker: Sand Rider
dialogueInline.text: Gone three years.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: And if he never comes back?

dialogueInline.speaker: Older Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: We don't know that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: You don't have to know it to live tomorrow.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: They kept the chair because moving it would make the loss real.

title: The Signet
summary: An elder presses Diaz's old signet into Brandon's hand as proof of office. Brandon refuses the object and returns it to the community rather than performing ownership of Diaz's authority.

panelPlan.text: An elder opens a small wrapped bundle containing a worn signet or command token carried since Diaz disappeared.
He places it in Brandon's palm before Brandon can refuse.
Brandon examines the ordinary worn object, then closes the elder's hand back around it.
He places the token in the center of the communal table where neither faction controls it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Older Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: He carried this. If you are Diaz, take it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm not.

dialogueInline.speaker: Older Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: Then tell us what to do with it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Keep it as his. Stop using it as mine.

title: No General
summary: Brandon turns the community's need for Diaz back on them: if they cannot choose without him, his return would only postpone the same fight.

panelPlan.text: The two factions face each other without Brandon between them. Jessie has the rig ready but does not rush the moment.
Brandon points to the vote tally and the blood token as two facts that belong to Los Lagartos, not to him.
He asks what happens next time they disagree if Diaz is the only person allowed to resolve it.
One Lagarto removes the head chair from the table entirely.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: You already chose once.

dialogueInline.speaker: Older Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: Not all of us accepted it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then argue about the vote. Argue about who gets counted. Argue about the promise Diaz made.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: But don't make a stranger do your arguing for you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: You can disagree without pretending the disagreement belongs to somebody absent.

title: The Vote Stands
summary: Los Lagartos decide that the prior vote will stand provisionally while they rewrite who has standing in future decisions. The result is theirs, imperfect and human, rather than Diaz's judgment.

panelPlan.text: The camp debates without looking at Brandon for permission. Voices overlap, but the social center has shifted back inside the community.
An elder proposes accepting the elected leader through the next route season while a broader count is negotiated before the following vote.
The blood claimant does not celebrate, but agrees not to challenge the decision by force.
Brandon quietly retrieves his canteen. Eva realizes he has become irrelevant to the decision and smiles at that rather than at a victory.

dialogueInline.speaker: Older Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: One season. Then we count again with the rule written first.

dialogueInline.speaker: Younger Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: One season, and everybody traveling with us gets heard before the count.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sand Rider
dialogueInline.text: That sounds like work.

dialogueInline.speaker: Older Lagarto
dialogueInline.text: It is ours.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: They stopped asking you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Best thing they've done all day.

title: The Preacher Arrived First
summary: As the trio prepares to leave, Eva learns that a traveling preacher arrived three days earlier and described not just Diaz's appearance but the fact that he would deny being Diaz.

panelPlan.text: Eva helps Sand Rider retie a load near the rig and asks exactly who told the camp Diaz was returning.
Sand Rider describes a weathered preacher who listened more than he spoke, then gave a careful prediction before leaving.
Jessie stops loading when she hears that the preacher predicted the denial.
Brandon asks whether the man gave a name. Sand Rider cannot swear to it; the preacher did not stay long.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Who told you Diaz was coming?

dialogueInline.speaker: Sand Rider
dialogueInline.text: Preacher passed through three days ago.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: What exactly did he say?

dialogueInline.speaker: Sand Rider
dialogueInline.text: Black hair. Dark coat. Travels with two others. He'd deny the name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That last part matters.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Did he give you his?

dialogueInline.speaker: Sand Rider
dialogueInline.text: Samuel, maybe. I remember the sermon better than the introduction.

title: A Useful Detail
summary: On the road out of Cinder Basin, Eva separates what could be coincidence from the one detail that strongly implies somebody prepared the encounter.

panelPlan.text: The rig climbs out of Cinder Basin while the camp shrinks behind them.
Eva lists the appearance details one by one; Jessie dismisses each as broad enough to travel by rumor.
Eva reaches the prediction that Brandon would deny the name. Jessie cannot dismiss that as easily.
Brandon resists converting the lead into certainty about motive or coordination.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Black hair is nothing. Dark coat is almost nothing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Traveling with us narrows it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Denying the name narrows it a lot.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: It tells us somebody expected me. It doesn't tell us why.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: It tells us where to start looking.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: For a preacher who may be named Samuel in the whole Sunfields.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Still better than four names and no person.

title: A Name in the Dust
summary: The trio leaves with its first concrete lead. Raina remains behind at Cinder Basin, confirming that another person is tracking the same pattern without yet explaining her role in it.

panelPlan.text: Eva writes SAMUEL? in her cheap notebook beneath BRANNOCK and DIAZ, leaving room rather than drawing a conclusion.
Jessie glances back through the dust and sees Raina standing where the camp road narrows.
Brandon does not turn around; he watches the road ahead.
Final wide panel: the rig moves into hard white distance while Raina remains a small ordinary human figure beside a dark exposed rib. No supernatural emphasis.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Raina isn't following.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Not yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then enjoy it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You know she has two names we don't.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I also know we're leaving.

title: Next: A SHADOW ON THE GLASS
settingText: A road town at dusk with a narrow stair descending into darkness beneath street level. Farther down the road, a lone traveler silhouette is already walking away from camera. No readable signage and no face detail.
summary: Art-directed closing teaser splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 2. Point directly at the next loaded pressure without revealing its resolution.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ART-DIRECTED SPLASH. Use one cinematic illustration rather than sequential panels. Reserve a large, deliberately quiet field for the supplied editorial body copy. The illustration supports the text without depicting the next issue's reveal literally.

LETTERING LAYOUT. Treat the supplied CAPTION lines as designed editorial typography, not speech balloons: strong heading, readable body copy, generous leading and margins, and a prominent final hook line. Do not invent any additional text, logos, signage, credits or slogans.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Somebody knew Brandon was coming.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Black hair. Dark coat.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And one particularly useful detail:

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: he would deny the name.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That is not how accidents work.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Somewhere ahead is a preacher who has been talking.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The next place on the road has a rule about names.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: NEXT: A SHADOW ON THE GLASS
